guide.title: Fenbendazole
guide.description: A veterinary dewormer with mixed cancer-model findings, unproven human anticancer benefit and documented liver-injury cases.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Cancer benefit: Not established. Human anticancer claims remain anecdotal. The human reports cited here describe liver injury rather than controlled cancer treatment. The selected cell and mouse studies have mixed findings and do not establish a human cancer regimen.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Cancer benefit: Not established. Human anticancer claims remain anecdotal. The human reports cited here describe liver injury rather than controlled cancer treatment. The selected cell and mouse studies have mixed findings and do not establish a human cancer regimen. Models only. Confidence in clinical translation: Low. In Gao 2008, lymphoma tumors in mice were smaller with fenbendazole plus supplemented vitamins (P = 0.009). Fenbendazole alone did not differ significantly from control (P = 0.12). The combination result cannot be attributed to fenbendazole alone, and nonsignificance does not prove equivalence.

questions.question: What do the animal experiments show?
questions.answer: Models only. Confidence in clinical translation: Low. Duan 2012 found no change in EMT6 mouse mammary-tumor growth, invasion, metastasis or response to local radiation with fenbendazole-containing chow. Duan 2013 also found no improvement in tumor growth or radiation response with intensive regimens. Those authors concluded that their experiments provided no evidence of value in cancer therapy; these findings apply to the tested models, not every possible cancer or regimen.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Safety evidence: Low for estimating frequency or individual risk. A 2024 case report described biopsy-confirmed severe liver injury after self-administration, with liver tests returning to normal after cessation. This is a serious human safety signal, but a case report cannot estimate how often it occurs.

sections.label: Contraindications
sections.paragraph: Human contraindication guidance: Not established by these studies. The human liver-injury reports identify harm after self-administration, but do not define a validated list of contraindications or a group in whom fenbendazole is safe.

sections.label: Interactions
sections.paragraph: Safety evidence: Low. A patient receiving nivolumab/relatlimab developed severe liver injury after increasing self-administered fenbendazole. The report distinguished suspected drug injury from immune-mediated hepatitis. It does not establish the size or mechanism of an interaction, or provide a safe combination schedule.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.paragraph: Human cancer dose: Not established. The cited cell and mouse studies do not establish a dose, duration or monitoring schedule for people. Human liver-injury reports do not define a safe threshold.

sections.label: Results
sections.paragraph: Models only. Confidence in clinical translation: Low. Dogra 2018 reported slower A549 lung-cancer xenograft growth in mice. This positive result is specific to that model and regimen, and cannot establish benefit in people or across cancers.

sections.paragraph: Official context: The cited FDA approval concerns an animal oral suspension and its labeled species. It does not assess veterinary products as human cancer medicines.

sections.label: Status
sections.paragraph: Official context: Fenbendazole is not FDA-approved for human use, including cancer treatment. In January 2026, the FDA approved a generic fenbendazole oral suspension for specified parasite infections in cattle and goats.

summary.text: Models only. Confidence in clinical translation: Low. In lung-cancer models, fenbendazole partly disrupted microtubules, interfered with cell division and increased cell death. These laboratory findings explain a research hypothesis; they do not show that an effective exposure can be reached safely in people.

questions.title: Are p53 and glucose effects consistent?
questions.text: Models only. Confidence in clinical translation: Low. Dogra reported p53 activation and reduced glucose uptake in lung-cancer cells. The pathway is not consistent across models: Park found no change in glucose consumption or lactate production in H4IIE rat liver-cancer cells, and a separate colorectal-cell abstract reported effects that did not require p53.
